# uor-repo-naming Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Repository naming and topic coverage: Decide whether a UOR Foundation repository follows the STANDARDS.md naming conventions and carries every Domain and Technology topic tag that applies to it, naming a broken convention before a missed preference.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never conformant when case is other

The app SHALL NOT answer `conformant` when case is other, because a name that is not lowercase and hyphen-separated never conforms.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `other absent preferred conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `conformant`
- **AND** the app answers `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never conformant when version is present

The app SHALL NOT answer `conformant` when version is present, because a version number belongs in a tag, never in the name.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase present preferred conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `conformant`
- **AND** the app answers `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never conformant when commits is other

The app SHALL NOT answer `conformant` when commits is other, because commits that are not Conventional Commits never conform.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent preferred conforming other complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `conformant`
- **AND** the app answers `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never conformant when domain is incomplete

The app SHALL NOT answer `conformant` when domain is incomplete, because a missing Domain tag never conforms.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent preferred conforming conventional incomplete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `conformant`
- **AND** the app answers `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never conformant when pattern is other

The app SHALL NOT answer `conformant` when pattern is other, because a name outside the preferred form is at best advisory.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `conformant`
- **AND** the app answers `advisory`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: Always advisory when case is lowercase and version is absent and branches is conforming and commits is conventional and domain is complete and technology is complete and pattern is other

The app SHALL answer `advisory` when case is lowercase and version is absent and branches is conforming and commits is conventional and domain is complete and technology is complete and pattern is other, because only the preference is missed, so the answer is advisory.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `advisory`
- **AND** the app answers `advisory`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-001 nonconforming when case is other

The app SHALL answer `nonconforming` when case is other, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Naming Conventions: repository names are all lowercase, hyphen-separated.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `other absent preferred conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 nonconforming when version is present

The app SHALL answer `nonconforming` when version is present and no earlier rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Naming Conventions: no version numbers in repo names (use tags).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase present preferred conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 nonconforming when branches is other

The app SHALL answer `nonconforming` when branches is other and no earlier rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Naming Conventions: branch names are {type}/{issue#}-{short-description}.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent preferred other conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 nonconforming when commits is other

The app SHALL answer `nonconforming` when commits is other and no earlier rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Naming Conventions: commit messages follow Conventional Commits v1.0.0.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent preferred conforming other complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 nonconforming when domain is incomplete

The app SHALL answer `nonconforming` when domain is incomplete and no earlier rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Topic Tags: every repository carries all Domain tags that apply.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent preferred conforming conventional incomplete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 nonconforming when technology is incomplete

The app SHALL answer `nonconforming` when technology is incomplete and no earlier rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Topic Tags: every repository carries the Technology tags of its primary languages.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete incomplete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 advisory when pattern is other

The app SHALL answer `advisory` when pattern is other and no earlier rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) Naming Conventions: the preferred form is uor-{domain}-{function}.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `advisory`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: Otherwise conformant

The app SHALL answer `conformant` when no rule matches, because STANDARDS.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8): every naming convention, the preferred form and the Domain and Technology tag rules are followed.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent preferred conforming conventional complete complete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `conformant`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete incomplete` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nonconforming`, decided by REQ-006, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 7 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `nonconforming`, `advisory`, `conformant`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `case` | `lowercase`, `other` | whether the repository name is all lowercase and hyphen-separated |
| `version` | `absent`, `present` | whether the repository name contains a version number |
| `pattern` | `preferred`, `other` | whether the name has the preferred form uor-{domain}-{function} |
| `branches` | `conforming`, `other` | whether every branch other than the default is named {type}/{issue#}-{short-description} |
| `commits` | `conventional`, `other` | whether every commit message on the default branch follows Conventional Commits 1.0.0 |
| `domain` | `complete`, `incomplete` | whether the repository carries every Domain topic tag that applies to it: math, cryptography, computation, visualisation, documentation, governance, protocol |
| `technology` | `complete`, `incomplete` | whether the repository carries a Technology topic tag for each of its primary languages: rust, python, typescript, lean4, coq, latex |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `nonconforming` | a naming convention or a required topic tag is not followed |
| `advisory` | every convention is followed, but the name is not in the preferred uor-{domain}-{function} form |
| `conformant` | every naming convention, preference and topic tag rule is followed |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 7 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `lowercase absent preferred conforming conventional complete complete` gives `conformant`
- `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete complete` gives `advisory`
- `other absent preferred conforming conventional complete complete` gives `nonconforming`
- `lowercase present preferred conforming conventional complete complete` gives `nonconforming`
- `lowercase absent preferred other conventional complete complete` gives `nonconforming`
- `lowercase absent preferred conforming other complete complete` gives `nonconforming`
- `lowercase absent preferred conforming conventional incomplete complete` gives `nonconforming`
- `lowercase absent other conforming conventional complete incomplete` gives `nonconforming`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
